clue.text: Reservoir sited in a good position

blocks.note: a well is a reservoir of water sunk into the ground
sited means put in a particular spot

explanation.surface: A description of where a reservoir has been built: somewhere sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-placed is located advantageously, so the phrase means situated in a favourable spot.

clue.text: Old boy dipping into untidy drawer for clothes

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside something, so one piece sits within the other
an untidy thing has been messed about, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word drawer jumbled, with a gap left for the inserted piece
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil rummaging in a messy chest of drawers looking for something to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's wardrobe is their whole collection of garments, so the word stands for one's clothes.

clue.text: Spanish girl almost caught by yobs seen on a rugby pitch?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped
caught by means held inside, so the shortened name goes within the other word

blocks.note: louts are yobs, rough uncouth young men
Ines is a common Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman nearly grabbed by hooligans at a rugby ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A line-out restarts play in rugby union: the forwards line up and the ball is thrown in between them from touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Line-outs are set pieces in rugby, so they are things one sees happening on the field during a match.

clue.text: Ample librarian, unlikely dancer

indicators.note: unlikely suggests something improbable or strange, so the letters are taken in an unexpected order

blocks.note: both words supply every letter for rearranging

explanation.surface: A buxom librarian is an improbable candidate for the ballet stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima ballerina is the leading female performer in a ballet company, so she is a dancer.

clue.text: Gobsmacked when odd tune is off-key

indicators.note: off-key means out of tune or wrong, so these letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
both words jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone shocked when a strange melody is played out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly amazed. 'Odd' looks like part of the picture but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone utterly amazed and lost for words; they are synonyms for great surprise.

clue.text: Last to fire put down an antelope

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the following word only

blocks.note: the closing letter of fire
to land is to put down, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: An instruction to shoot an antelope, the final shot putting it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests killing the animal, but here it means bring to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African species of antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Policeman lashing back of offender with whip

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
lashing means tying round something, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: cop is slang for a police officer
the closing letter of offender

explanation.surface: An officer flogging a criminal's backside with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashing' fits the whip picture, but it means binding around.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short whip used by horse riders, so the word names that kind of whip.

clue.text: Former president and eastern commander protected by Royal Navy

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded by it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy
E for eastern, a compass point
an aga is a Turkish military commander

explanation.surface: An ex-president and an oriental general guarded by British sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Aga (also agha) is the Ottoman title for a commander, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan served as the fortieth US president in the 1980s, so he is a former holder of that office.

clue.text: Old man getting support of girl, Spanish dish

indicators.note: in a down entry the support is what lies underneath, so the second piece comes after the first

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An elderly father leaning on a young woman for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Valencian rice dish cooked with saffron, seafood or meat, a national food of Spain.

clue.text: Wise sayings, saws from Pole, I'd translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: Proverbs from a Polish speaker that someone claims to have rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: A saw is an old proverb, which makes the fodder look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls of wisdom are wise remarks or pieces of advice, often said ironically, matching sage sayings.

clue.text: Grow profusely in rubbish round collapsed ruin

indicators.note: a collapsed building is in pieces, so the letters fall into a new order
round means surrounding, so the first word goes about the second

blocks.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
the word ruin jumbled

explanation.surface: Weeds spreading wildly over the debris around a fallen-down ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that run riot spread uncontrollably, an idiom for growing abundantly and wildly.

clue.text: A girl, for example, having come back in par

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the abbreviation runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
Vera is a girl's name
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A golfing woman who has returned to form, playing at par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Par' suggests golf, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or typical level, as in 'up to par', which is the ordinary middle standard.

clue.text: Girl giving letter from Greece to District Attorney

blocks.note: rho is the Greek letter R
DA is the US abbreviation for district attorney

explanation.surface: A young woman handing a letter sent from Greece to a prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: In a yacht from Ireland, us at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A crew sailing from Ireland, out on the open water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the yachting picture perfectly but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel under sail is moving by wind power, so travelling under sail means being aboard a sailing boat.

clue.text: Group storing its floats with miscellaneous items

indicators.note: storing means keeping something inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people
taken as written
something that bobs floats up and down on water

explanation.surface: A carnival group keeping its parade floats along with other assorted gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floats' reads as carnival vehicles, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits and bobs is an informal British idiom for assorted small things or odds and ends.

clue.text: Extra run leads to defeat?

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, an additional run scored when a fielder's throw passes the stumps
second meaning: removal from power by force

explanation.surface: A sports remark that giving away one more run costs the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run gained because a fielder's throw at the stumps goes past them is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bonus cricket run from a wayward throw and a toppling or defeat of a ruler.

clue.text: Lie about king causes conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the abbreviation

blocks.note: a fiction is an untruth
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A falsehood concerning a monarch stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction means disagreement or tension between people, which is a form of strife or discord.

clue.text: Film big names round elevated green

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word up means reading it bottom to top
round means encircling, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: stars are celebrities, big names
green means raw, inexperienced or unripe

explanation.surface: A movie whose famous cast stand around a raised lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's 1977 space-opera movie, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Said by courteous males (flirts aside, possibly)?

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, so the letters can be reordered

blocks.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Polite men, setting any flirting aside, say a gallant phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside in the surface but holds the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlemen say this when letting women go ahead of them through a door, a phrase of old-fashioned politeness.

clue.text: Wager about unfavourable living quarters

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: a bet is a wager
ill can mean unfavourable, as in ill omen

explanation.surface: A bet placed on poor accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging assigned to a soldier, often in a private house, so it is accommodation.

clue.text: Twist artist during trip

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so the abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: a spin is a short trip, as in a car
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter wrenching an ankle while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' suggests stumbling, which fits a twisted ankle, but it means a jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist a joint is to wrench it and injure the ligaments, which is exactly the verb used here.

clue.text: Eminent fellow drinking wine in it

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the second word goes inside the first
in places the combined piece within the final word

blocks.note: taken as written
a man is a fellow
port is a fortified Portuguese wine

explanation.surface: A distinguished chap knocking back a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An important person is one of high standing and influence, which is what a distinguished or prominent person is.

clue.text: A university study identifies US poet born in Britain

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: Academic research reveals a poet's transatlantic origins.
explanation.walkthrough: W H Auden was born in York and later took American citizenship.
explanation.definitionFit: W H Auden, born in York in 1907, moved to America in 1939 and became a US citizen.

clue.text: Suffer at home with scoundrel

blocks.note: in means at home
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Having to endure living with a rogue under the same roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and undergo it, a sense of suffer.

clue.text: Piece of legislation brought in is widely read

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of legislation
money brought in has been earned

explanation.surface: A new law introduced by someone well versed in the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of legislation' looks like a whole phrase meaning an act, but only one letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person has studied a great deal, so they are scholarly and well read.

clue.text: Famous Soviet skater in bar accompanied by girl

blocks.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
Nina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A celebrated ice skater out at a pub with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Irina Rodnina won three Olympic pairs figure-skating titles for the USSR in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Irina Rodnina is a renowned Soviet pairs figure skater with three Olympic gold medals.

clue.text: Very small container by yard

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A little receptacle sitting next to a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means minute or extremely little, so it is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Undecided, like Dr Jekyll at times?

blocks.note: first meaning: unable to choose between options
second meaning, playful: Stevenson's doctor shares his head with Mr Hyde, so he literally has a double mentality

explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's story, Dr Jekyll turns into the evil Mr Hyde, so he houses two separate personalities.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wavering between choices, and taken literally it fits a man with a split personality.
